latest_release.name: v1.18.0
latest_release.body: ## Features > [!WARNING] > The submodules of `trl.experimental.async_grpo` are gone. `from trl.experimental.async_grpo.async_grpo_config import AsyncGRPOConfig`, and imports from `async_rollout_worker`, `packing`, `vllm_client` or `weight_transfer` in that package, no longer work. Import the trainer from `trl`, the rollout loop from `trl.trainer.async_grpo_trainer`, and the vLLM client from `trl.generation.async_vllm_client` (renamed `AsyncVLLMClient`). `from trl.experimental.async_grpo import AsyncGRPOConfig, AsyncGRPOTrainer` still works, with a `FutureWarning`, until v2.0.0. ### :mortar_board: `AsyncGRPOTrainer` is now a stable trainer `AsyncGRPOTrainer` runs GRPO with generation decoupled from training. A rollout worker in a background process streams completions from a vLLM server, scores them and queues them, while the training loop pulls from the queue and updates the model. Generation and gradient updates overlap instead of alternating, and the trainer sends its new weights to the server over NCCL every `weight_sync_steps` steps. In v1.17 it lived in `trl.experimental.async_grpo`: seven files, three ways to batch and bound generation, two constructor arguments for swapping out internals, and metric names that didn't match GRPO's. This cycle cleaned that up in about 40 PRs, tracked in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/7841: config renames, one timeout instead of three, one batching mode, generation held to `max_staleness`, GRPO's metric names and init checks, a public rollout loop, and the two-file layout every stable trainer has. Then https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/8288 moved it to the top-level package. ```python # Before from trl.experimental.async_grpo import AsyncGRPOConfig, AsyncGRPOTrainer # Now from trl import AsyncGRPOConfig, AsyncGRPOTrainer ``` The old path still works and emits a `FutureWarning` (removal in v2.0.0). The rollout loop extension point lives next to the trainer, `from trl.trainer.async_grpo_trainer import AsyncRolloutLoop, Rollout`, and isn't exported from `trl`. The OpenEnv / Harbor harness stays experimental, as `HarnessAsyncGRPOTrainer` in `trl.experimental.async_grpo.openenv_harness`. Logged metric names can still change between releases. Quick start, from the [docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/async_grpo_trainer). Install with `pip install trl[vllm,kernels,math_verify]`, then start the vLLM server on GPU 0: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B \ --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl"}' \ --logprobs-mode processed_logprobs \ --api-server-count 8 \ --max-model-len 4096 ``` Then train on GPU 1 with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python train_async_grpo.py`: ```python # train_async_grpo.py from datasets import load_dataset from trl import AsyncGRPOTrainer from trl.rewards import accuracy_reward if __name__ == "__main__": # the rollout worker is a spawned process that re-imports this script dataset = load_dataset("trl-lib/DeepMath-103K", split="train") trainer = AsyncGRPOTrainer( model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B", reward_funcs=accuracy_reward, train_dataset=dataset, ) trainer.train() ``` This exact example runs end to end. It's a sanity check, not a speedup comparison: | | | | --- | --- | | Model / data / reward | `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B`, `trl-lib/DeepMath-103K`, `accuracy_reward` | | Hardware | 2x B200: vLLM on one GPU, the trainer on the other | | Config | default `AsyncGRPOConfig`: fp32 weights with bf16 autocast, 8 generations per prompt, up to 2048 completion tokens, `token_budget` read from `--max-model-len 4096` | | Step time | ~7 s/step, after ~5 min of warmup | | Throughput | ~7k trained tokens/s | | Trainer vs vLLM log-prob gap | 0.007 to 0.02 | What
